children: Meta Platforms Inc Class A (NASDAQ:META) is doubling down on AI with Muse and acquisitions while cutting jobs and facing talent departures, regulatory limits on teen use, data-center tax headwinds and mixed analyst views as investors weigh adoption, cost savings and near-term sentiment.
Previous Week Recap
Meta Launches Muse Personal AI
: META launched Muse, a personal AI agent on app, web, WhatsApp, iOS, Android; uses secure VM, accesses email, calendar, payments, smart‑home; free plus $20/$100 plans; shares rose ~5–6.6%.
META Shifts To AI, Cuts Jobs
: Meta Platforms (META) shifts resources to AI and is cutting thousands of jobs; company began layoffs in March 2026. Traders: watch potential cost savings, AI investment and execution risk.
META Declares Quarterly Dividend
: Meta Platforms (META) declared a $0.53 quarterly cash dividend per Class A share, payable September 28, 2026. Record and ex‑dividend dates were not specified in the announcement.
KeyBanc Cuts META Target
: KeyBanc cut Meta Platforms (META) price target to $760 from $855, citing Muse Spark progress but needing clearer proof of adoption, Hatch value, and MTIA-driven cost cuts.
Facebook, Instagram Under-18 Limits

: Settlement limits Facebook and Instagram use for under-18s: 2-hour daily cap and midnight–6 a.m. block. Under-18 users ~1% of Meta Platforms Class A (META) revenue — minimal near-term revenue impact.
ARK Buys Meta Shares
: ARK Invest bought ~43,091 Meta Platforms (META) shares for about $27.9M across two ETFs, timed with Meta’s AI push including Muse assistant and Stilla.ai acquisition.
META AI Researcher Exits
: Meta Platforms (META) sees AI researcher Andrew Tulloch depart after ~11 years, leaving for Anthropic. Traders: monitor potential talent turnover and any short-term sentiment impact on META shares.
TikTok Blocks META Ads
: TikTok refused to run Meta Platforms Inc Class A (META) paid ads tied to a campaign pressuring settlements, signaling a change in how a major platform handled META ad placements.
Consumer AI Push On Meta
: T. Rowe Price’s Tony Wang says Meta Platforms (META) can use Instagram, Facebook and WhatsApp to deploy consumer AI agents and exploit user context in the competing AI agent market.
States Cut Data-Center Breaks
: States cutting data‑center tax breaks have prompted changes impacting Meta Platforms Inc Class A (META), affecting planned or existing data‑center investments and potential tax costs.
